name: Vansen Pressline Work Henley
description:
A heavy-duty three-button henley made for people who work with their hands. The fabric is Vansen's signature GritWeave — a dense synth-cotton composite that resists minor abrasions and holds up to repeated industrial washing without pilling or fading. Raglan sleeves allow full arm mobility, and the reinforced shoulder panels are triple-stitched. Comes in two colors: off-white and a dark charcoal called 'Forge.' The chest pocket is sized to hold a data chip or a folded work order.

Vansen makes workwear the way workwear should be made — without frills. The Pressline Henley is issued to workers at several Tier 2 manufacturing floors as optional uniform-adjacent clothing, which means you see it everywhere from assembly lines to freight yards to the weekend market.
what_it_says: You work for a living and you're not embarrassed about it. You buy clothes that last, not clothes that impress.
story_hooks: The charcoal colorway has become an informal identifier for members of a Tier 2 labor organizing cell — wearing it to a meeting means you're sympathetic.
A character wears one as a disguise to blend into a factory floor they have no business being on.
Someone finds a work order folded in the chest pocket of a secondhand one — the job listed was never completed.
